_about: Rake layer, applied to every chart when the table has a rake (the Play tab's 5% capped at 3bb), after the stack depth layer and before the low-stakes layer. Rules have the same form as lowstakes.json: each moves a share ('scale') of one action's weight to another for the listed hands. 'keys' limits a rule to chart entries whose key matches one of them (a trailing '*' matches any ending); without it the rule applies to every entry of its spot. The rake is taken only from pots that see a flop, so it taxes hands that win small pots after the flop and leaves pots won before the flop alone: the blinds defend tighter, thin cold calls and the weakest steals fold more, and the big blind 3-bets a little more of its best calls. All values are estimates, not solver output.

rules.note: The rake comes out of every pot that sees a flop, so the big blind defends fewer weak offsuit and low suited hands.
Pots won before the flop are not raked, so the big blind 3-bets a little more of its best calling hands.

rules.hands: 66-22, A9s-A6s, K9s, Q9s, J9s, T8s, 87s, 76s, 65s, 54s, ATo, KJo
rules.note: Cold calls with small pairs, suited connectors and weak aces win mostly small pots after the flop, which the rake taxes, so make fewer of them.

rules.hands: K4s-K2s, Q5s-Q2s, J5s-J4s, T6s, 96s, 85s, 74s, 63s, 53s, 43s, A4o-A2o, K8o, Q9o, J8o, T8o, 98o, 87o
rules.note: When the weakest steals get called, the pot is raked, so open a little tighter from the late seats.
Limped pots are small and still pay rake, so over-limp half as often.
